schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE customers
(
    CustomerID INTEGER UNIQUE     not null
        primary key,
    Segment    TEXT null,
    Currency   TEXT null
);

CREATE TABLE gasstations
(
    GasStationID INTEGER    UNIQUE   not null
        primary key,
    ChainID      INTEGER          null,
    Country      TEXT null,
    Segment      TEXT null
);

CREATE TABLE products
(
    ProductID   INTEGER   UNIQUE      not null
        primary key,
    Description TEXT null
);

CREATE TABLE "transactions_1k"
(
    TransactionID INTEGER
        primary key autoincrement,
    Date          DATE,
    Time          TEXT,
    CustomerID    INTEGER,
    CardID        INTEGER,
    GasStationID  INTEGER,
    ProductID     INTEGER,
    Amount        INTEGER,
    Price         REAL
);

CREATE TABLE "yearmonth"
(
    CustomerID  INTEGER not null
        references customers
            on update cascade on delete cascade
        references customers,
    Date        TEXT    not null,
    Consumption REAL,
    primary key (Date, CustomerID)
);
q1: SELECT GasStationID FROM transactions_1k GROUP BY GasStationID ORDER BY SUM(Price) DESC LIMIT 1
q2: SELECT GasStationID FROM transactions_1k GROUP BY GasStationID ORDER BY SUM(Price * Amount) DESC LIMIT 1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT GasStationID FROM transactions_1k GROUP BY GasStationID ORDER BY SUM(Price) DESC LIMIT 1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT GasStationID FROM transactions_1k GROUP BY GasStationID ORDER BY SUM(Price * Amount) DESC LIMIT 1
counterexample:
INSERT INTO transactions_1k (TransactionID, Date, Time, CustomerID, CardID, GasStationID, ProductID, Amount, Price) VALUES (1, '2023-01-01', '08:00', 1, 100, 1, 1, 10, 5.0);
INSERT INTO transactions_1k (TransactionID, Date, Time, CustomerID, CardID, GasStationID, ProductID, Amount, Price) VALUES (2, '2023-01-01', '09:00', 2, 200, 2, 2, 1, 100.0);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 orders gas stations by the SUM of Price per transaction (i.e., total price paid per transaction across all rows), whereas Q2 orders by SUM(Price * Amount), which computes the total monetary value spent at each gas station (price per unit multiplied by quantity). These two aggregations can yield different results depending on the values of Amount and Price.
counterexample_dsp: A gas station with a single high-price transaction and low amount vs. another with many low-price transactions and high amounts will yield different results between Q1 and Q2.
